$comment: Generated by `npm run manifest`. Do not edit by hand: change the code, tokens, CLAUDE.md or manifest/usage.md.
name: Slot
description: The allow-list for building with Slot: use only the components, props, values and tokens listed here, and follow the rules.

components.name: Button
components.description: An action the user can take.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual emphasis: primary, secondary or danger (destructive).

props.name: size
props.description: Height 36 / 48 / 56.

props.name: children
props.description: The label. Sentence case.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Figma Disabled state. Native attribute.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the single child (e.g. a link) with button styles instead of a <button>.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: Renders a native <button> with type="button" by default, so it never submits a form by accident.
Disabled uses the native attribute: the button leaves the tab order and is announced as unavailable.
Focus ring: 2px border-focus outline, 2px from the button (transparent gap), on :focus-visible only.

usage.purpose: Triggers an action: submitting, saving, confirming, opening a dialog. The variant tells the user how important or risky the action is.
useWhen: `primary`: the main action of a screen, form or dialog ("Book now", "Save changes"). At most one primary button per area.
`secondary`: alternative or less important actions next to a primary one ("Back", "Keep booking"), or actions on a screen that has no single main action.
`danger`: the action destroys or cancels something and can't easily be undone ("Cancel booking", "Delete account"). Usually confirmed in a Dialog first.
`size`: `medium` by default; `large` for the main action on a sparse screen or a touch-first layout; `small` in dense layouts, next to other small controls.
dontUseWhen: The action navigates to another page: use a link, or a Button with `asChild` wrapping the link, so it is announced as a link.
The control selects an option: use RadioGroup or Select (one choice) or Chip (filters).
You need a red button for emphasis rather than a destructive action: `danger` means destructive only.
Two `primary` buttons would sit side by side: make one `secondary`.

components.name: Card
components.description: A bordered container that groups related content under a title.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title, Heading/Small.

props.name: elevation
props.description: flat = border only; raised = border plus the raised shadow.

props.name: children
props.description: Content slot, stacked with space-2.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: Title renders as an <h2>; check the heading order on the screen (Heading/Large page title is the <h1>).
A plain <div>, not a landmark, so a list of cards doesn't flood the landmark list.

usage.purpose: Groups related content under a title so it reads as one unit, e.g. a booking summary.
useWhen: `flat`: the default, inside a page that already has structure (a list of bookings, a summary in a form).
`raised`: the card sits on a busy or tinted background, or needs to stand out from other content on the screen.
Several items of the same kind appear in a list or grid, each with a title.
dontUseWhen: The content is the whole page: use the page layout and a Heading/Large title instead.
You only need spacing between sections: use space tokens, not a border.
The content needs the user's decision before continuing: use Dialog.
You would nest a card inside a card.

components.name: Chip
components.description: A toggle button for filtering or picking options, shown as a 36px pill.

props.name: children
props.description: The label. Sentence case, one or two words.

props.name: selected
props.description: Figma Selected state (controlled). Rendered as aria-pressed.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Initial selected state when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Figma Disabled state. Native attribute.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: A native <button> with aria-pressed reflecting `selected`; screen readers announce it as a toggle button.
Selected is shown by colour and announced by aria-pressed, never by colour alone.
Group related chips in a labelled container (e.g. role="group" with aria-label).

usage.purpose: Toggles a filter on or off. Each chip is independent, so the user can turn on several at once, e.g. filtering services by type.
useWhen: Filtering content: each chip turns one filter on or off, and several can be on at the same time.
Changing a chip updates the content immediately, without a submit button.
The filters are short (one or two words) and few enough to show in one row or two.
dontUseWhen: The user must choose exactly one option: use RadioGroup (2 to 5 options) or Select (a longer list, or when space is tight).
The chip triggers an action rather than a state: use Button.
The chip is a read-only label or status: Slot has no badge yet; don't use a disabled Chip for it.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: A modal window that asks the user to confirm or decide before continuing.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions, right-aligned. Always include a visible dismiss action, wrapped in DialogClose.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional extra content between the description and the footer.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Element that opens the dialog, e.g. a Button. Optional when `open` is controlled.

accessibility: role="dialog", labelled by the title and described by the description; the rest of the page is aria-hidden while open.
Focus moves into the dialog on open, is trapped while open, and returns to the trigger on close.
Escape and an overlay click close it. There is no close (×) button, so the footer must always contain a visible dismiss action.

usage.purpose: Interrupts the current task to ask for a decision or confirmation that must happen before the user continues.
useWhen: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action ("Cancel booking?"), with a `secondary` Button to dismiss and a `danger` or `primary` Button to confirm.
A short, focused decision or input that belongs to the current screen and can't be skipped.
dontUseWhen: Showing information that doesn't need a decision (success messages, tips): show it inline on the page.
The content is long, a multi-step flow or a full form: use a page.
The action is easy to undo: just do it, and offer undo inline if needed.
Opening a dialog from inside another dialog.
The footer has no visible dismiss action: Slot dialogs have no close (×) button, so a dismiss action ("Keep booking", "Cancel") is required.

components.name: Disclosure
components.description: A row with a summary and optional detail line that expands to show more content below it.

props.name: summary
props.description: The trigger text: a short summary of what expands. Sentence case.

props.name: detail
props.description: Optional second line under the summary, Body/Small in text-secondary.

props.name: open
props.description: Figma Open state (controlled).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initially open when uncontrolled.

props.name: children
props.description: Content slot, shown when open, stacked with space-3.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: The trigger is a native <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the content.
The visible summary and detail line are the button's accessible name (no aria-label, so the name always contains the visible text), so it should make sense on its own; the chevron is decorative.
Closed content is removed from the accessibility tree, so don't put the only copy of required information inside.

usage.purpose: Shows a summary (and an optional detail line) that the user can expand to see more below it, e.g. a compact booking summary on mobile.
useWhen: Secondary detail that most people don't need to read every time, but some will want to check (the full booking details on a small screen).
The `summary` makes sense on its own when collapsed; with `detail`, the two read as one name ("Deep tissue massage", "Tue 4 Nov, 10:00 · $95"). Together they are the button's accessible name.
Use `detail` for a second, secondary line instead of letting one long summary wrap.
Closed by default; use `defaultOpen` (or `open`) only when most people will need the content.
dontUseWhen: The content is required to complete the task (a form field, a terms checkbox): show it.
The content needs a decision before continuing: use Dialog.
There's room to show everything (e.g. desktop with a side column): show a Card instead.
You'd nest a Disclosure inside a Card, or a Disclosure inside a Disclosure.

components.name: Icon
components.description: A 20px Lucide icon in the Slot icon colours.

props.name: name
props.description: Lucide icon name, as in the Figma Icon variants.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Use the icon-disabled colour.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: Decorative by default (aria-hidden). Pass aria-label to make it a meaningful image (role="img").

usage.purpose: A small Lucide glyph that supports a label or shows state, in the Slot icon colours. Only the icons in the Figma Icon component are available.
useWhen: Reinforcing meaning next to text (a check next to a selected option, a chevron that opens a menu).
An icon-only control has an accessible name (`aria-label` on the control or the icon).
dontUseWhen: The icon would be the only way to convey meaning, with no text or accessible name.
The icon you need isn't in `name`'s allowed values: add it to the Figma Icon component first, then to the code; don't import another Lucide icon directly.
Decoration only, with no meaning: leave it out.

components.name: Input
components.description: A single-line text field with label and helper text, 48px tall.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, Label/Small.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Example input shown while empty. Never a replacement for the label.

props.name: helper
props.description: Helper text under the field; turns error red when invalid.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Figma Error state. Rendered as aria-invalid.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Figma Disabled state. Native attribute.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: The label is a <label for>, so clicking it focuses the field and screen readers announce it.
Helper text is linked with aria-describedby; in the Error state it should say how to fix the problem.
Error sets aria-invalid; helper text stays text-secondary when disabled (WCAG contrast).

usage.purpose: A single-line text field for free text the user types, such as a name or email, with a label and optional helper text.
useWhen: The answer is free text or a number that can't be picked from a known list.
Always with a visible `label`; add `helper` when the format or purpose isn't obvious.
`invalid` when validation fails, with `helper` saying how to fix it.
dontUseWhen: The answer comes from a known list: use RadioGroup (2 to 5 options) or Select (more, or when space is tight).
The text may span more than one line (notes, messages): use Textarea.
You'd use `placeholder` instead of `label`: placeholders disappear while typing and aren't a label.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.description: Choose exactly one of 2 to 5 options, all visible at once.

props.name: options
props.description: The choices, in display order. 2 to 5 options.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label, Label/Small. Names the radiogroup.

props.name: helper
props.description: Helper text under the options; turns error red when invalid.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected value (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initially selected value when uncontrolled.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Figma Error state. Rendered as aria-invalid on the group.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Figma Disabled state. Disables every option.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: role="radiogroup" labelled by the group label; helper text is linked with aria-describedby, so the error message is read with the group; Error sets aria-invalid on the group.
Errors are group-level (left bar + message), never on individual options; the bar is not the only signal, the message says what to fix.
Keyboard: one Tab stop for the group; arrow keys move between options and select them; Space selects the focused option.
Each option is a role="radio" button named by its <label>; clicking the label selects it.

parts.name: RadioGroupItem
parts.description: One option: the radio circle and its label. RadioGroup renders these from `options`; use directly only to compose a custom group.

usage.purpose: Chooses exactly one of 2 to 5 options, all visible at once, e.g. the appointment type.
useWhen: The user must choose exactly one option, and there are 2 to 5 of them.
Seeing every option side by side helps the user compare before choosing.
Inside a form, with a group `label`, and `helper` when the choice needs explaining.
`invalid` with a `helper` message saying what to fix, when the group fails validation. Group-level errors use a left bar and a message; individual options are never marked as errors.
dontUseWhen: There are more than 5 options, or space is tight: use Select.
The user can choose several options, or is toggling filters: use Chip.
There is only one option to switch on or off: Slot has no checkbox or switch yet; don't use a one-option RadioGroup.
Choosing an option should trigger an action immediately: use Button.

components.name: Select
components.description: Pick one option from a list, in a 48px field with a menu.

props.name: options
props.description: The choices, in display order.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, Label/Small.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while no option is selected.

props.name: helper
props.description: Helper text under the field; turns error red when invalid.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Figma Error state. Rendered as aria-invalid.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Figma Disabled state. Native attribute.

accessibility: The field is a combobox labelled by the <label>; helper text is linked with aria-describedby.
Keyboard: Enter, Space or arrows open the menu, arrows move, Enter selects, Escape closes.
While open, the menu is modal: focus is trapped in it, the rest of the page is aria-hidden and the field leaves the tab order; focus returns to the field on close.

parts.name: SelectItem
parts.description: One option row in the Select menu. Select renders these from `options`; use directly only to compose a custom Select.

usage.purpose: Picks exactly one value from a list of predefined options, in a compact field that fits in a form.
useWhen: The user picks exactly one value and there are more than 5 options.
Space is tight (e.g. a dense form or a narrow column), even with 5 or fewer options.
Inside a form, alongside Inputs, with a visible `label` and optional `helper`.
dontUseWhen: There are 2 to 5 options and there is room to show them: use RadioGroup, so every option is visible without opening a menu.
The user can pick several values, or is toggling filters: use Chip.
The list is very long or needs search: Slot has no combobox with search yet.
Selecting an option should trigger an action or navigation immediately: use Button.

components.name: Textarea
components.description: A multi-line text field with label and helper text, at least 120px tall.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, Label/Small.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Example input shown while empty. Never a replacement for the label.

props.name: helper
props.description: Helper text under the field; turns error red when invalid.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Figma Error state. Rendered as aria-invalid.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Figma Disabled state. Native attribute.

inherits.note: Other props pass through to the rendered element (e.g. aria-*, onClick, className).

accessibility: The label is a <label for>, so clicking it focuses the field and screen readers announce it.
Helper text is linked with aria-describedby; in the Error state it should say how to fix the problem.
Error sets aria-invalid; helper text stays text-secondary when disabled (WCAG contrast).
Mark optional fields in the label ("(optional)"), not only in the helper.

usage.purpose: A multi-line text field for longer free text, such as notes or a message, with a label and optional helper text.
useWhen: The answer is free text that may run to more than one line ("Notes for your therapist").
Always with a visible `label`; mark optional fields in the label ("(optional)"), and add `helper` to say what kind of text helps.
`invalid` when validation fails, with `helper` saying how to fix it.
dontUseWhen: The answer is a single line (a name, email, phone number): use Input.
The answer comes from a known list: use RadioGroup or Select.
You'd use `placeholder` instead of `label`: placeholders disappear while typing and aren't a label.

semantic.name: color/action/danger
semantic.job: Background for destructive actions, e.g. a Danger button.

semantic.name: color/action/danger-hover
semantic.job: Background for destructive actions on hover.

semantic.name: color/action/disabled
semantic.job: Background for filled actions that are disabled, e.g. a disabled Primary button.

semantic.name: color/action/primary
semantic.job: Background for the main action, e.g. a Primary button.

semantic.name: color/action/primary-hover
semantic.job: Background for the main action on hover.

semantic.name: color/action/secondary
semantic.job: Background for secondary actions and unselected toggles, e.g. a Secondary button or a chip.

semantic.name: color/action/secondary-hover
semantic.job: Background for secondary actions and unselected toggles or radios on hover.

semantic.name: color/action/selected
semantic.job: Background for a chosen option: a selected chip or a checked radio.

semantic.name: color/action/selected-hover
semantic.job: Background for a checked radio on hover.

semantic.name: color/border/action
semantic.job: Border for secondary actions, e.g. a Secondary button.

semantic.name: color/border/action-hover
semantic.job: Border for secondary actions and unselected toggles on hover, e.g. a hovered Secondary button or chip.

semantic.name: color/border/control
semantic.job: Border for unselected toggles and choice controls, e.g. chips and radios.

semantic.name: color/border/disabled
semantic.job: Border for disabled fields and controls.

semantic.name: color/border/error
semantic.job: Border or marker for a field or group with an error.

semantic.name: color/border/field
semantic.job: Border for text fields and selects at rest.

semantic.name: color/border/focus
semantic.job: Keyboard focus ring, and the border of a focused or open field.

semantic.name: color/border/selected
semantic.job: Border for a chosen option: a selected chip or a checked radio; also previews the choice on a hovered radio.

semantic.name: color/border/selected-hover
semantic.job: Border for a checked radio on hover.

semantic.name: color/border/subtle
semantic.job: Quiet outline that separates a container from the page, e.g. cards, menus and dialogs.

semantic.name: color/icon/default
semantic.job: Icons at rest.

semantic.name: color/icon/disabled
semantic.job: Icons and marks in disabled controls, e.g. the dot of a disabled selected radio.

semantic.name: color/icon/on-action
semantic.job: Icon or mark drawn on an action fill, e.g. the radio dot or a checkbox check.

semantic.name: color/shadow/raised
semantic.job: Shadow under raised surfaces, e.g. raised cards, menus and dialogs.

semantic.name: color/surface/disabled
semantic.job: Background for disabled fields and controls.

semantic.name: color/surface/field
semantic.job: Background for text fields, selects and unselected radios.

semantic.name: color/surface/hover
semantic.job: Background of a hovered interactive row, e.g. a menu option or a disclosure summary.

semantic.name: color/surface/overlay
semantic.job: Scrim behind a dialog that dims the page.

semantic.name: color/surface/page
semantic.job: Background for the page and for content areas that sit on it, e.g. cards, menus and dialogs; also the gap in the focus ring.

semantic.name: color/surface/selected
semantic.job: Background for the selected row in a menu or list.

semantic.name: color/text/action
semantic.job: Label of secondary actions, e.g. a Secondary button.

semantic.name: color/text/action-hover
semantic.job: Label of secondary actions and unselected toggles on hover.

semantic.name: color/text/disabled
semantic.job: Text and labels in disabled fields and controls.

semantic.name: color/text/error
semantic.job: Error messages, e.g. helper text in the Error state.

semantic.name: color/text/on-action
semantic.job: Text on a filled action or selected toggle, e.g. a Primary button or selected chip label.

semantic.name: color/text/on-disabled
semantic.job: Text on a disabled filled action, e.g. a disabled Primary button label.

semantic.name: color/text/placeholder
semantic.job: Placeholder text in empty fields and selects.

semantic.name: color/text/primary
semantic.job: Main text: titles, labels, body copy and field values.

semantic.name: color/text/secondary
semantic.job: Supporting text: helper text, descriptions and captions.

tokens.note: Colours: semantic tokens only (colour primitives are not for direct use). Spacing, radius, type and borders: the scales.

rules: Text styles use Title Case with slash groups by role and size (e.g. `Label/Medium`, `Label/Small`, `Body/Medium`).
Use Heading/Large once per screen, for the page title. Section and card titles use Heading/Small.
Helper text always uses text/secondary, including in disabled states.
UI copy uses sentence case (e.g. "Save changes", not "Save Changes").
For components with borders, exclude strokes from layout.

Verify component heights match the size scale: **36 / 48 / 56**. The scale applies to controls with a background or border box (Button, Input, Select, Chip). Radio rows are 24px (20px circle + Body/Medium line); stacked with space/3 they repeat every 36px.
Nested corners: inner radius = outer radius minus padding.

Error indicators that mark a whole group sit outside the group's box, so showing them never shifts or indents content. (Radio Group: the bar is 14px left of the content, border/width/2 + space/3; containers must leave that space unclipped. Form columns have at least 16px of margin on mobile.)

Components only use Slot CSS variables from `src/styles/tokens.css`. Never hex, `rgb()`, `oklch()` or other literal colors, and never Tailwind default colors (`bg-slate-500`, `text-white`, …). The default palette is removed in `src/index.css`, so those classes don't exist.
Prefer **semantic** tokens (`--color-text-primary`, `--color-action-primary`) over primitives (`--color-blue-600`).

Use Tailwind's variable syntax: `bg-(--color-action-primary)`, `text-(--color-text-primary)`, `p-(--space-4)`, `gap-(--space-2)`, `rounded-(--radius-md)`, `border-(length:--border-width-1)`, `text-(length:--font-size-body)`.
shadcn utility names (`bg-primary`, `border-input`, `ring-ring`, …) are allowed: they are mapped to Slot semantic tokens in `src/index.css`.

Component props use the Figma property names, with the Figma values lowercased (e.g. Figma `size` = `Small | Medium | Large` → `size?: 'small' | 'medium' | 'large'`). Prop values are always lowercase, even though Figma variant values are Title Case.
Check the component in Figma (`get_design_context`) before writing or changing its props.
`Default`, `Hover` and `Focus` are CSS (`:hover`, `:focus-visible`), not props.
`Disabled` is the native `disabled` attribute.
`Error` is an `invalid` prop, rendered as `aria-invalid`.
`Selected` is a `selected` prop. `Open` is an `open` prop.
Other variant properties map 1:1 to lowercase props with lowercase values (`variant`, `size`, …).
Figma strokes are inside and excluded from layout, so draw borders with `inset-ring-*` (box-shadow), not `border`, to keep Figma padding and the 36 / 48 / 56 heights.

In code, focus rings use outline + outline-offset, so they work on any background: `focus-visible:outline-solid focus-visible:outline-(length:--border-width-2) focus-visible:outline-offset-(length:--border-width-2) focus-visible:outline-(--color-border-focus)`. (Figma keeps the two drop shadows; same geometry.) `outline-solid` is needed because components set `outline-none`.

`manifest/usage.md` holds when to use each component. Only the repo owner changes an entry's `Status:` to `Approved`. Agents always write `Status: DRAFT - needs review`: for every new entry, and when they change an existing entry, even one that was Approved.
Name only components, props and prop values that exist in the manifest (`npm run manifest` fails otherwise). Name things Slot doesn't have in lowercase ("Slot has no checkbox yet").
A dialog without a close button must always have a visible dismiss action, and must close on Escape.
